assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window with a cubic-kilometre detector built in Antarctic ice is the kind of instrument-driven discovery I weigh most heavily. The 2013 evidence for a diffuse high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux, followed by the 2017 TXS 0506+056 association and the NGC 1068 and Galactic-plane results, founded neutrino astronomy. The detector concept, calibration of the ice and the systematics work are decisive and durable.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the IceCube programme; Karle was central to construction, deployment and the instrument's performance. Spiering is credited for early AMANDA/IceCube leadership and could be an alternative, so the allocation among the three is not obviously unique. A fair two- or three-person configuration is feasible, but the collaboration is large and the AMANDA-to-IceCube lineage complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux independently seen in several analyses and, in part, by other channels. Source identification is still limited to a few objects, with KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD only beginning to confirm. Recognition is arguably timely but the source-physics story is still maturing.
uncertainties: Source population of the diffuse flux remains largely unidentified
Evidence for individual sources (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) is at roughly 3-4 sigma level and awaits further confirmation
Whether the Nobel should name AMANDA pioneers beyond the three credited people is unresolved

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, via the magic-wavelength idea, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, far beyond the caesium standard, and enables tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a redefinition of the second. This is precision instrumentation with a clear measurable payoff, which fits my own criteria of control of systematics and independent reproduction.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock; Ye made the decisive precision advances at JILA, including the quantum-degenerate clocks. Two laureates is a clean and fair configuration. Ion-clock and frequency-comb contributors were recognised earlier (2005, 2012), so overlap is limited.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced and compared clocks at the 1e-18 level; the technology is mature, with international comparisons and a pending redefinition of the second. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for frequency combs and ion trapping may make some committee members regard it as an incremental extension
Credit for the magic-wavelength concept versus later accuracy records could be debated by other contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction and the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter. Originality and impact are very high, and the combination of theory prediction and decisive experiment is a classic prize pattern. I lean on colleagues for the condensed-matter detail.
assessment.attribution: MacDonald and Bistritzer made the theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experiments. The supplied credit supports a three-person prize, although Cory Dean, Kim and others who contributed to the moire platform are not in the credited names, so some will argue the allocation is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups worldwide, with a rapidly growing literature including fractional Chern insulators. The basic phenomenon is well established, but the nature of the superconducting pairing is not settled, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated
Credit for related moire and 2D-heterostructure experiments outside the credited names
Possible preference to wait for an application-level or definitive many-body result

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed-light injection in gravitational-wave interferometers now improves the sensitivity of LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA and demonstrates quantum noise reduction in a flagship instrument. As an instrument builder I value a theoretical idea that became routine in a large detector. Impact is high, but the physics is quantum optics applied to an observatory already honoured in 2017.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the 1981 proposal; Kimble's group made the first squeezed-light demonstrations in 1985-86 with Slusher's group at Bell Labs also pivotal; Mavalvala and Schnabel were central to implementing it in the detectors. The credit is genuinely contested and four named people plus others exceed a three-person prize, which is a significant allocation problem. My proposed set is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Implemented and operated in GEO600 and in the LIGO/Virgo detectors for several observing runs, so the confirmation is strong and independent. Timing is fine.
uncertainties: Slusher and Bell Labs colleagues are not in the credited names, so the 1980s experimental credit may be incomplete
Four credited people with distinct roles cannot all be honoured
Possible perception that it is a sub-component of the 2017 LIGO prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correcting spherical aberration brought sub-angstrom resolution and atomic-scale chemical and structural imaging to routine electron microscopy, widely used across materials science and physics. It is a textbook detector-and-optics invention: a long-standing theoretical limit overcome by careful engineering. The 2008 Wolf Prize recognised the same trio.
assessment.attribution: Rose provided the theory of the corrector, Haider built and demonstrated the first corrected TEM, and Urban developed the application to materials; this three-way split is natural and commonly accepted, so attribution is comparatively clean.
assessment.maturity: Aberration correctors are commercial and in use in laboratories worldwide, so the technology is thoroughly confirmed. If anything, the main question is timing since some members might say it belongs to chemistry or has been overtaken by cryo-EM recognition in 2017.
uncertainties: Fit to physics versus chemistry/materials science may be questioned
Contributions of Crewe, Krivanek and others to aberration correction could be raised

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and E91 launched quantum cryptography, with secure key distribution whose security rests on the laws of quantum mechanics rather than computational assumptions. It is conceptually original and now realised in fibre and satellite links. Colleagues in quantum information can judge the foundations better than I can, but the practical relevance to secure communication is evident.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the clear originators of BB84; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is a distinct contribution. Three people is natural, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding idea is a known credit issue and he is not among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations including satellite QKD are numerous and independent, but real-world security against device imperfections is still being worked out. The 2022 prize to Aspect, Clauser and Zeilinger already honoured Bell tests and entanglement, which reduces novelty for the committee.
uncertainties: Wiesner's contribution is not covered by the credited names
Overlap with the 2022 prize may weigh against it
Practical device-level security remains an open engineering question

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable arrays of single neutral atoms with Rydberg blockade have enabled quantum simulation of many-body spin models at scales of hundreds of qubits, and have progressed to error-corrected logical-qubit demonstrations. The experimental control and detection techniques are impressive. In atomic and quantum-information topics I defer to colleagues' reviews.
assessment.attribution: Browaeys and Lukin both drove the experimental realisation of the arrays, while Saffman contributed the Rydberg-blockade gate proposal and early experiments. Others, such as Bernien, Endres and Weiss, did key work and are not credited, and the 2001 Jaksch-Zoller theory is another claimant. Allocation is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent groups replicate the platform and it is evolving fast. Applications to quantum computing remain unproven at scale, so it may be premature for a prize.
uncertainties: Several key contributors are missing from the credited names
Quantum-computing relevance still unproven
Rapid progress could change who is seen as decisive

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors underpin the vertex and tracking systems of every major collider experiment, including those that discovered the Higgs boson, and have spread to medical and photon-science imaging. This is the type of detector invention I know well; the impact is vast and lasting. The 1992 Charpak prize recognised gas detectors, so there is precedent for detector prizes.
assessment.attribution: Parker's microstrip work, and the Heijne-Jarron hybrid-pixel developments at CERN, are decisive, but the field is very collaborative, with many others such as Hallewell, Kemmer, Rancoita and later Medipix and ATLAS groups. A clean three-person split is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature technology confirmed across numerous experiments and time-tested over decades. Timing is late rather than premature, which is not a barrier.
uncertainties: Large collaborative lineage, including Kemmer's planar process, may not be captured by the credited trio
Committee may regard detector instrumentation as less discovery-oriented
